```{r q2a-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr); library(readr); library(stringr); library(knitr); library(kableExtra)
```

```{r q2a-run, include=FALSE}
source("B_Q2a_select_top3.R")

fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
latex_escape <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("\\\\", "\\\\textbackslash{}", x)
  x <- gsub("([%&#_$])", "\\\\\\1", x)
  x <- gsub("\\{", "\\\\{", x); x <- gsub("\\}", "\\\\}", x)
  x <- gsub("~", "\\\\textasciitilde{}", x)
  gsub("\\^", "\\\\textasciicircum{}", x)
}
q2a <- read_csv("outputs_B/B_Q2a_top3_posts.csv", show_col_types = FALSE,
                locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"))
r   <- r_counts
n_explicit <- sum(str_starts(review_candidates$content_assessment, "Explicit"))

status_sentence <- switch(status_state,
  match       = "These counts match the handoff status file.",
  not_checked = "The handoff status file was not available for an automatic count check.",
  mismatch    = "WARNING: these counts differ from the handoff status file.")
handoff_sentence <- if (handoff_match) {
  "The result is identical to the team handoff file in URIs, order, text, author, period and engagement counts."
} else {
  "WARNING: the result differs from the team handoff file."
}
```

## Question 2(a): Selection of the three most-replied-to posts

**Method.** Threads were selected from the Question 1 topic dataset, which contains `r fmt(validation$value[1])` posts labelled as event-related (`r fmt(validation$value[2])` Before and `r fmt(validation$value[3])` After). `r status_sentence` Posts were ranked by `reply_count`, the reply count reported by the Bluesky API at collection time. Likes and then the post URI were used as tie-breakers, but `r if (tie_at_boundary) "a tie occurred" else "no tie occurred"` at the third position (`r r[3]` versus `r r[4]` replies). `r handoff_sentence` Each selected post and its replies form one discussion thread (T1 to T3).

```{r q2a-table-metrics}
q2a %>%
  select(Thread, Author, Period, `Created (UTC)`, Replies, Likes, Reposts,
         `Label source`) %>%
  kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
        caption = paste("The three most-replied-to posts in the Question 1 topic",
                        "dataset (n = 4,536). Engagement counts as reported by the",
                        "Bluesky API at collection time.")) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position", "scale_down"), font_size = 9)
```

```{r q2a-table-text}
q2a %>%
  mutate(Text = latex_escape(Text), URL = paste0("\\url{", URL, "}")) %>%
  select(Thread, Text, URL) %>%
  kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
        caption = "Original text and Bluesky URL of the three selected posts.") %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position", "scale_down"), font_size = 8) %>%
  column_spec(1, width = "1.1cm") %>%
  column_spec(2, width = "7.2cm") %>%
  column_spec(3, width = "6.6cm")
```

**Results and relevance.** T1 received `r r[1]` replies, `r round(r[1] / r[2], 1)` times as many as T2 (`r r[2]`) and `r round(r[1] / r[3], 1)` times as many as T3 (`r r[3]`). T1 is the only Before-period post. The account `bsky.app` posted it two hours before the 17:00 UTC cut-off between the two periods, and its text refers to "today's Apple event". T2 and T3 were posted after the event and mention the iPhone Duo.

All three posts were included by the keyword rules (`label_source = rule_based`). No `manual_event_label` is recorded for any of them, even though `r validation$value[9]` topic posts carry a recorded human label. A provisional content inspection by Owner B, which is not recorded as a label, confirms that each text explicitly mentions the Apple event or the iPhone Duo. The intent of T1 is nevertheless ambiguous. A later post by the same account inside the thread refers to the Honeycrisp apple variety. One reply within the thread reads: "They're talking about the fruit. It's a joke thread."^[Reply URI: \url{`r quote_check$reply_uri[1]`}] The selected threads are therefore the most-replied-to posts that reference the event. They are not necessarily the most substantive product discussions.

**Limitations.** Reply counts are API snapshots from a sample that depends on the search queries, not a census of Bluesky. The retrieved English-declared replies (`r paste(thread_replies$retrieved_replies, collapse = ", ")` for T1 to T3) include nested replies and exclude empty or non-English-declared replies. They therefore differ from `reply_count`; Question 2(b) uses the retrieved replies.

The selection also depends on the Question 1 relevance rules. A total of `r nrow(review_candidates)` posts outside the topic dataset have at least `r r[3]` replies (listed in `B_Q2a_review_candidates.csv`). Provisional inspection found that `r n_explicit` of them explicitly refer to the event or the announcement. Relabelling those posts would replace T3 with `r sub("^.*; ", "", scenarios$top3[2])` and leave T1 unchanged. The current labels are retained until the group confirms these readings.
